title: IRGC Announces 26 Vessels Transited Hormuz in 24 Hours Under Iranian Coordination
detail: The IRGC Navy announced it had coordinated the transit of 26 vessels — tankers, container ships, and other commercial vessels — through the Strait of Hormuz over the previous 24 hours. The figure represented a significant increase from the near-zero commercial transit levels since Iran closed the strait in late February 2026. Iran framed the announcement as a demonstration of its sovereign control over the waterway, asserting that all transit requires Iranian coordination and approval. Meanwhile, US-Iran negotiations on establishing a permanent Hormuz transit mechanism remained stalled, with the US calling Iran's demand to impose transit tolls 'unfeasible.' Global shipping continued to avoid the strait as a war risk zone, adding 10–14 days to voyages via the Cape of Good Hope.

media.caption: IRGC Navy says it coordinated the crossing of 26 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz in a 24-hour period

title: Iran Warns of Wider Retaliation; Pakistan Intensifies Peace Mediation
detail: The IRGC issued a formal warning that any renewed US-Israeli aggression would 'expand the war beyond the region, with powerful strikes from unexpected fronts.' Parliament Speaker Qalibaf and FM Araghchi echoed these warnings, signaling Iran's deterrent posture remained robust despite the ongoing ceasefire. Simultaneously, Pakistani Interior Minister Naqvi made his second visit to Tehran in less than a week to advance the Islamabad-brokered peace mediation process, deepening Pakistan's diplomatic role as the primary channel between Washington and Tehran. Pakistan's intensive mediation — following from the ceasefire framework it helped broker in April 2026 — reflected Islamabad's strategic interest in de-escalating a conflict on its western and northwestern borders.

media.caption: Iran warns of expanded retaliation while Pakistan intensifies mediation efforts in Tehran

title: Iran's Internet Blackout Reaches 82 Days — Only Elite and Business Access Maintained
detail: As Iran's internet shutdown for ordinary citizens reached its 82nd day, Euronews published a detailed analysis of the 'class internet' system that had emerged: government officials, approved businesses, and intelligence services retained tiered VPN-enabled access while the general public remained cut off. The internet shutdown was imposed on February 28, 2026, when US-Israeli attacks began, and had become one of the longest national internet shutdowns in modern history. President Pezeshkian's committee to study restoration — announced May 15 — was widely seen as cosmetic given the IRGC's effective veto over cyberspace policy. The shutdown was causing severe economic damage to small businesses, e-commerce, and remote workers, compounding Iran's war-related economic contraction.

media.caption: Tehran's tiered internet leaves most Iranians in the dark 82 days into the war-era internet blackout
